summary: Coalesced token batches delivered on resume after brief SSE disconnect causing merged partial choices
description: Issue summary: Customer observed that after a short SSE disconnect (~1–2s) their streaming response resumed but the first resumed chunk merged the last partial tokens from before the disconnect with the next tokens, producing an invalid merged token boundary and a malformed JSON choice in the final output. Impact: Customer-facing chat UI shows corrupted/merged fragments for 2–3% of resumed sessions during recent hours. Environment: Production; dedicated cluster in us-east serving redwood-v1-13b for NeuroDocs tenant. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start streaming generation for prompt that yields multi-choice JSON output with forced choice delimiters. 2) Simulate network hiccup causing SSE stream to drop for ~1–3 seconds (client reconnects automatically). 3) Observe first resumed chunk contains concatenated gif-token fragments and an extra comma that breaks downstream JSON parse. Observed behavior: On resume the resumed chunk content begins with tail fragment from previous chunk immediately followed by the next chunk's tokens with no clear delimiter. Example extracted from logs: "[2026-03-13T16:04:28.522Z] TX last_chunk_offset=1824 body='...\"partial_choice_1_end\"'" and then "[2026-03-13T16:04:30.731Z] RESUME chunk_offset=1825 body='\"partial_choice_1_end\",\"choice_2_start\"'" Expected behavior: Resumed chunks should preserve original token boundaries or emit a deterministic resume marker so clients can stitch without merging tokens. Temporary workaround: Advise customer to enable strict reparse using choice indices from metadata (if available) and to retry fetch of the last N tokens from the non-streaming endpoint as a fallback.
steps_to_reproduce: Start SSE stream for multi-choice JSON generation on redwood-v1-13b
Introduce a 1-3s network drop between client and edge (simulate flaky mobile network)
Allow client to auto-reconnect and consume resumed chunks
Observe first resumed message for merged token boundary causing JSON parse failure

comments: 2026-03-13 17:02 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Assigned to SRE to validate resume semantics and check kernel for batch coalescing during short reconnects.

2026-03-13 17:35 - SRE (Marco Li): Reproduced locally by simulating proxy half-close. Initial hypothesis: continuous-batcher may coalesce buffered fragments across resume boundary when ACK window is delayed by the proxy. Collected debug trace from edge logs.
2026-03-13 18:20 - Customer (Ops lead, NeuroDocs): Confirmed behavior occurs intermittently in production. We see it across multiple users and only when reconnects are under ~3s.
2026-03-13 19:05 - SRE (Marco Li): Added temporary flag on the dedicated cluster to emit explicit RESUME_MARKER events on resume; asking customer to validate if the marker allows safe reassembly.

2026-03-13 21:11 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer validated that with RESUME_MARKER enabled they can reassemble and parse successfully. Marker added as short-term mitigation while we investigate root cause.

2026-03-14 09:08 - Runtime (Anya Petrov): Replayed kernel-level traces; found that the continuous-batcher's flush-on-disconnect path can append remaining buffer to first resumed payload when proxy ACKs arrive out-of-order. Creating PR to ensure discrete boundary events are emitted and buffer is flushed into separate chunks with resume metadata. Linking PR in investigation notes.
investigation_notes: Captured pcap and edge debug: ACK window timing shows 110–320ms variance causing batch flush to be deferred until resume handler runs.

Continuous-batcher behavior: when buffer is non-empty and connection reset occurs, batched fragments may be concatenated into next transmit when resume rebind completes. Observed 'concat' at service-layer rather than client-locally due to missing resume delimiter.
Reproduce steps validated on staging with overloaded proxy; increasing keepalive frequency reduces incidence. This suggests race on ACK/flush path with proxy half-close behavior.
Related to earlier ticket SUP-330412 (delayed-ack-window) but new in that malformed tokens are produced by coalescing rather than missing final chunk
resolution: Mitigation applied: Enabled RESUME_MARKER emission on dedicated cluster for NeuroDocs and other affected tenants - customer confirmed parsing restored.

Code fix: PR opened to modify continuous-batcher flush semantics so that any buffered fragments are emitted as a distinct resume chunk and annotated with resume_offset metadata (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284).
Deploy plan: Canary merge to staging, run synthetic reconnect load for 48h, then roll to prod with feature gate. Expected full production rollout 2026-03-18 pending canary results.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add automated test simulating proxy half-close/resume with ACK jitter. 2) Add metric for resumed-chunk-merge-rate in Console. 3) Update developer docs with recommended client-side stitch patterns and to recommend RESUME_MARKER usage.
